questions.stem: You are in a café and want to order a coffee politely.
questions.explanation: „Ich hätte gern“ is the polite way to order — softer than „ich will“. „Kaffee“ is masculine, and it is the object of the sentence, so the accusative article is „einen“.

build.translation: I would like a coffee, please.

questions.explanation: Starting with „heute“ pushes the subject after the verb, because the verb has to stay in second position. Keeping English order — „heute ich spiele“ — is the classic beginner mistake.

questions.stem: You want to say that you can play today.
questions.explanation: A modal verb takes second position and throws the other verb to the very end as an infinitive. English keeps the two together — 'I can play' — which is exactly the habit to break.

questions.stem: You are lost and need to ask a stranger the way to the station.
questions.explanation: „Zu“ always takes the dative, and it contracts: „zu dem“ becomes „zum“, „zu der“ becomes „zur“. Using „der Bahnhof“ here would leave the noun in the wrong case.
